title: Base44 / Wix Terms and Data-Use Evidence Intake
lead: Test the investigator-supplied quotations and summaries attributed to Base44/Wix terms, privacy documentation, Responsible Use Policy, security documentation, and Trust Center. The quoted materials are indexed as leads and are not treated as independently authenticated source captures.
journalist: AXIOM Journalist / AxiomZero Special Investigations Division

entities.name: Base44
entities.description: Platform named in the investigator-supplied terms and privacy excerpts.
entities.stated_position: Position excerpts supplied by the investigator; original pages not independently retrieved in this session.
entities.notes: No inference of unlawful surveillance or foreign-government access is established by the excerpts.

entities.name: Wix.com Ltd.
entities.description: Identified in the supplied Terms preamble as the operator of Base44-branded services.
entities.stated_position: Attributed Terms excerpts are in the source bundle; operator response not separately requested or received.
entities.notes: Corporate identity and the exact current contracting entity require confirmation against the live agreement.

entities.name: Base44 subprocessor directory
entities.description: Trust Center directory reported by the investigator to list 36 vendors and processing locations.
entities.notes: No dated directory capture or complete vendor roster is attached.

entities.name: Decart
entities.description: Named in the supplied Trust Center summary as an Israel-based LLM API subprocessor.
entities.notes: Subprocessor scope is unverified. No evidence here establishes military tasking, access to all user data, or transfer of military technology.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.description: Named in the supplied Trust Center summary as a U.S.-based LLM API subprocessor.
entities.notes: No acquisition attempt or specific user-payload routing is established by this intake.

entities.name: Amazon Web Services
entities.description: Named in the supplied Trust Center summary as a U.S.-based infrastructure vendor.
entities.notes: The entry does not establish an Azure-to-AWS migration of any military workload.

sources.title: Base44 Trust Center — subprocessors and vendor risk

open_questions: Can the original dated Base44 pages and Trust Center directory be retrieved or supplied as immutable exports with retrieval timestamp and hashes?
What exact language and opt-out procedure appear in the entire arbitration provision, and what jurisdiction and consumer statutes govern?
Which customer data categories are used for AI training on each plan, by Base44 and each model vendor, and what opt-out, retention, and deletion controls apply?
What is the complete dated 36-vendor subprocessor list, and for each vendor what data, purpose, region, retention, onward subprocessor, and access role are disclosed?
Does Decart receive prompts or payloads from Base44 in actual production, or is it merely listed as an available processor? What do the applicable DPA and service configuration say?
Where does TLS terminate, which data are decrypted for processing, who can access encryption keys, and what is the scope/date of the SOC 2 and ISO certifications?
What exact contents, configuration and trigger does the Trust Center backup/data-retention schedule specify?
Have Wix/Base44 been asked to confirm the supplied passages, describe actual practice, and respond to the questions above?
